clips.send: MORTISE and TENON. Dovetail tenon. A tenon shaped like a swallow’s tail, dropped in from above. Through tenon. Dovetail. The tail is wider at the end, so once it drops in, the beam cannot be pulled out sideways. Clever: the harder you pull, the tighter it locks. Mortise-and-tenon is ancient: the Hemudu people used it in their stilt houses about 7,000 years ago.

clips.send: The Qin dynasty’s Lingqu (today: Xing’an, Guangxi) Canal used single water gates (陡门 dǒumén). In 984, under the Song, the official Qiao Weiyue built a lock with two gates near today’s Huai’an. It is often called one of the world’s first true locks, roughly 400 years before Europe’s (approximate).
